statement: For every prime p, the labelled cyclic p-root system has finitely many solutions and their total intersection multiplicity is binom(2p−2,p−1). The corresponding cyclic-sum map on (C*)^p is proper of that multiplicity. Distinct-root equality is not asserted for every prime.

answer.text: There are binom(2p−2,p−1) cyclic p-roots with multiplicity.
answer.multiplicity: Total intersection multiplicity; distinctness is not asserted.

notes:
Do not confuse ordinary real z-coordinates with unimodular cyclic roots/CAZAC sequences. All cyclic relabellings are counted.

scope: Labelled z=(z_0,...,z_(n−1))∈(C*)^n satisfying Σ_i z_i...z_(i+k−1)=0 for k=1,...,n−1 (indices modulo n), and ∏_i z_i=1; no symmetry quotient. Restrict n=p prime.
